Codelco has already reached an agreement with Japanese buyers to cut the annual premium to $85/t from $93/t in 2013, which means Chinese buyers will for ask at least the same $8/t decrease. A major trader in China told us that the majority of their customers, who are smaller copper traders, had cut their annual contract volumes for 2013. The contracts are drawn up based on Codelco’s annual benchmark price. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **November 2012** www.crugroup.com Both domestic spot and futures prices have remained largely unchanged in the last two weeks, due to there being no perceived pickup in demand. A better HSBC PMI reading for October indicates a small uptick in demand, but market sentiment has not yet reacted to this, with copper prices broadly flat in the last fortnight. The SHFE three-month copper prices increased to RMB56,090/t on 23rd November, up slightly from RMB55,930/t on 9th November. SHMET spot market prices fell marginally to RMB 55,700/t on 23rd November, down from RMB56,050/t on 9th November. End of picture text --> An article on 20th November suggesting that bonded stocks in China have reached the 1Mt mark has generated large amounts of interest. In CRU’s view this figure is too large and we do not agree that stocks have risen so dramatically in a such a short period of time. When speaking to multiple market participants, we gather information to gauge the total level of “visible” bonded stocks. These are the stocks held in bonded warehouses in Shanghai owned by warehousing companies, that anyone can deposit material into. While there are warehouses owned by private trading houses in the bonded areas of Shanghai, which hold so called “invisible” stocks, the levels of these stocks is much more opaque, very difficult to gauge and rarely quoted. Therefore, we believe that when the article referred to 1Mt of bonded stocks, it was excluding these invisible stocks, making it difficult for us to agree with this figure. From our regular conversations with senior traders in China, we estimate that Shanghai bonded cathode stocks have risen in late November, but only to between 700,000-750,000t; compared to between 650,000-700,000t in late October/early November. This has been largely fuelled by weaker domestic demand and more cargoes arriving in November. We also estimate that the stock levels in Guangdong province, mainly Nanhai and Guangzhou warehouses, remain unchanged from October at around 75,000t. However, market participants have told us that changes in Guangdong stock levels are generally small and do not attract market attention; none of the estimates we were given was remotely close to the 150,000t figure quoted in the article earlier this week. We agree that the stocks have increased recently, and are at a very high level, but from our ongoing conversations, we see only a gradual upward trend in November, and not a sudden jump. Therefore, our © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **November 2012** www.crugroup.com estimate of total stocks at bonded warehouses in China, Shanghai and Guangdong combined, are between 775,000-825,000t by 23rd November. # October imports experience seasonal fall Arbitrage favourable for imports

China’s refined copper imports fell 21.7% m-o-m to 230,690t in October, the lowest reading in 2012 so far. However, levels were not far short of those reported in July and August, and the downturn from September is in line with seasonal patterns. Bookings are brought forward to late September before the start of the holiday week in October, creating a spike in September and a fall in October. We note that

this did not occur last year due to significant price movements at the time, which drew scrap out of the market and drew in buyers of cathode  which resulted in an atypically strong October in 2011. 

According to a survey by the Shanghai Metals Market, operating rates at 21 Chinese producers of copper plate, sheet, strip and foil, with a capacity of 984,200t/y, fell to 56.40% in October, down 1.13 percentage points from September.  A second survey from SMM showed that operating rates at 21 Chinese wirerod producers, with a capacity of 3.5Mt/y, fell to 69.02% in October, a decline of 2.33% m-o-m, and 14.4% y-o-y.  Both these surveys also highlighted seasonal reasons for the downturn in output. 

In terms of the outlook for November, the arbitrage for the importing business has improved compared to early November (Chart 1), helping imports.  Additionally, large annual contract volumes, signed by Chinese buyers with overseas suppliers at the beginning of this year, should ensure cargoes will continue arriving at normal speed.  Therefore, we expect cathode imports to rebound accordingly in November. 

# Market after the party event 

China ended its seven-day 18<sup>th</sup> National Congress of the Communist Party of China on 14<sup>th</sup> November, and Xi Jinping was appointed as the new president of China.  As previously expected, there were no big announcements in terms of immediate economic stimulus during the party event, and the market remained relatively quiet.  Some market participants have said they expect the new group of leaders to introduce new policies next year, as part of putting their stamp on the role, but these are expected to be token policies rather than dramatic changes. 

The party congress did yield some longer term goals, which have long run market implications.  Outgoing president Hu Jintao said that the Chinese government will aim to double China’s per capita GDP by 2020 from 2010 levels.  The goal, which includes rural and urban households, will be supportive of sectors such as home appliances as the disposable income of the Chinese population rises.  A second

announcement, by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development-China, stated that China will continue tightening policies targeting the real estate industry.  Regardless of whether housing prices or sales volumes increase, the ministry said the government will issue controlling policies accordingly.  It was also announced that the Chinese government will construct at least 5M units of social housing in 2013, lower than this year’s 7M.  Under the government’s five year plan, 36M units of social housing are due to be constructed over the period 2011-2015; since 2011 the government has started or completed 17M units. 

Economic data released recently has shown some improvement, with the HSBS China PMI reaching 51.3 in November, the highest level since November

2011.  Additionally, China’s October vehicle sales rose 3 percent from the same period a year ago.  We are expecting the macroeconomic environment to improve through to the end of the year, and CRU’s economic forecast is for an increase in the Chinese GDP growth rate to 8.1% next year from 7.6% this year.
